messages:
Maria Chen: quick FYI — I'm handing off oncall to @Jon at 18:00 PT. leaving a few notes/questions so we don't have surprises. :wave:

Maria Chen: main ask: can we confirm responsibilities split for tonight's coverage? I'm thinking: SRE = infra/host/network/PD escalations; Runtime = model-serving software, model rollbacks, and runtime-level mitigations. comments?

Jon Patel: sounds right but who does a canary rollback for a model if it starts hallucinating in prod? runtime or SRE?

Lee Wong: runtime should own model rollbacks and config toggles (model version pinning, disabling tools). SRE should own infra rollbacks (kernel, instance types, networking). if it's mixed (eg GPU driver bug causing model errors) we coord and page both. :+1:

Ana Rodriguez: can we add a short escalation path for mixed issues? sometimes people ping the wrong PD and it adds latency.

Maria Chen: yes — proposed path:
```
1) Whoever detects: post to #eng-oncall + add the oncall PD (sre-oncall or runtime-oncall).
2) If it's clearly infra (host down, mounting issues, network) -> page SRE PD.
3) If it's clearly model/runtime (bad outputs, API schema break, model OOMs) -> page Runtime PD.
4) If uncertain or both impacted -> page SRE PD AND Runtime PD immediately and start a quick bridge in the channel.
5) If customer-facing or P0/P1 impact -> escalate to oncall manager (pager escalation policy step 2) and open incident doc.
```
Maria Chen: definitions we used tonight:
- Incident (P0/P1): any outage or customer-impacting regressions (API 5xxs, sustained latency > 3x baseline, major correctness regressions tied to model output where customers get wrong outputs at scale).
- Degradation (P2/P3): transient latency increase, single model misbehaving for < 10% of traffic, partial throttles.

Jon Patel: ok makes sense. One edge case: autoscale flapping causing higher latencies — infra or runtime?

Lee Wong: primarily infra (autoscaler, instance launch failures). but runtime should look for cache/kv leak patterns. coordinate.

Ana Rodriguez: for handoffs — can we add a simple checklist in the handoff message? last deploy, active canaries, known risk flags.

Maria Chen: good idea. leaving this as my handoff snippet for tonight:
```
- last_deploy: 2025-10-03T17:22:00Z (model-service v2.4.1)
- canaries: 5% traffic -> healthy
- open_risks: small increase in tokenization errors (tracking #eng-ml), one flaky GPU host (host-52) marked draining
- who_to_page: runtime-oncall (Jon Patel), sre-oncall (Lee Wong)
- runbook_refs: /runbooks/model-incident, /runbooks/infra-network
```

deploy-bot: Deploy completed: model-service v2.4.1 to prod at 2025-10-03T17:22:03Z :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall: added Jon to PD escalation for tonight and pinned Maria's handoff snippet to #eng-oncall.

Jon Patel: thanks — I'll watch the canaries for the next 2 hours and handle any model rollbacks. if I page SRE I'll include stack traces and host ids. :eyes:

Maria Chen: tiny procedural note: when paging, include the prefix `[SEV?]` and the short impact line e.g. `[P1] 50% of requests 5xx` — helps routing.

Ana Rodriguez: also please add a link to any relevant traces/logs in the first message so it's actionable.

Jon Patel: will do. thanks for the handoff, Maria. :thumbsup:

Maria Chen: thanks team — handing off now. ping me if anything unusual while I'm offline.

pagerduty-bot: Incident policy: oncall change recorded — Jon Patel primary for runtime PD tonight.

Lee Wong: one last reminder, if you see persistent >2x latency for >15min escalate to P1 per the policy.

Jon Patel: noted. starting watch.
